name: Menu and Menubar
description: A menu offers a list of choices (actions or functions), while a menubar is a visually persistent, typically horizontal menu providing consistent access to commands.

keyboard_interactions.action: Opens submenu and focuses first item; or activates item and closes menu
(Optional) Toggles menuitemcheckbox; checks menuitemradio; opens submenu; or activates item
In menubar: opens submenu. In menu: moves focus to next item
In menu: moves focus to previous item. In menubar (optional): opens submenu, focuses last item
In menubar: moves to next item. In submenu: opens child submenu or closes current and moves to next menubar item
In menubar: moves to previous item. In submenu: closes submenu, returns to parent
Closes the menu and returns focus to invoking element
(Optional) Moves focus to next item beginning with that character

required_attributes.description: false when hidden; true when visible

notes: role='menubar' models a DESKTOP APPLICATION menu bar (File, Edit, View). It is almost never correct on a website. See patterns/menu-button.md for the decision table — this is the same mistake, one level up.
Site navigation is <nav> + <ul> + <a>, with no ARIA. A menubar over site nav switches screen readers into application mode and breaks their normal reading keys.
Use it only when you are genuinely building an application menu bar in a web app — an editor, an IDE, a design tool.
It is one Tab stop, with roving tabindex. Left/Right move along the bar; Down opens a submenu and focuses its first item; Escape closes and returns to the bar.
Real focus moves (.focus()); do not use aria-activedescendant.
Submenus need aria-haspopup='menu' and aria-expanded on their parent menuitem.
Never make a hover-only submenu: it must open on Enter/Space/Down as well (RAWeb 7.3).
native_element: none — and for websites, the answer is almost always <nav> instead

raweb_criteria.reason: menubar/menu/menuitem roles, aria-haspopup and aria-expanded must all be exposed.
Full two-dimensional keyboard navigation: Left/Right across the bar, Up/Down into submenus, Escape out.
The focused menu item must be visibly indicated.
Closed submenus must be hidden from assistive technologies.
One Tab stop for the whole menubar; focus returns predictably on close.
Escape and Tab must always let the user out.
